claims.text: Adding yttrium oxide to a magnesium-based alloy can enhance its glass-forming ability.
The initial material is an amorphous magnesium-based alloy.
The proposed yttrium oxide addition is 5–10 at.%.
The proposed rapid-solidification cooling rate is 10^5 K/s.
Yttrium oxide forms or acts as nanoparticles in the magnesium-based alloy.
Yttrium oxide nanoparticles inhibit heterogeneous nucleation.
Adding yttrium oxide increases atomic packing density.
Heterogeneous-nucleation inhibition enhances the alloy's glass-forming ability.
Increased atomic packing density enhances the alloy's glass-forming ability.
Yttrium oxide addition is predicted to produce a 20% increase in glass-forming ability relative to the alloy without the addition.
The predicted enhancement is represented by an increase in the critical cooling rate.
The optimal yttrium oxide concentration and cooling rate may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the critical cooling rate does not increase by at least 15% relative to the baseline alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes enhanced glass-forming ability as an increase in critical cooling rate. Because improved glass-forming ability is ordinarily represented by a lower critical cooling rate, the stated outcome and falsification direction are inconsistent with the claimed enhancement.
